name: WheelPicker
description: A scrolling wheel picker with one or more columns, item snapping, a centred selection band, an optional 3D cylinder look, optional infinite looping, and a haptic-free selection callback. Drag, mouse wheel, keyboard arrows and tap-to-select all work.

fields.selectionColor: ThemedColor? - selection band fill; null = accent at 12% alpha
fields.selectionBorderColor: ThemedColor? - band border; null = border token
fields.foreground: ThemedColor? - selected row text; null = foreground token
fields.mutedForeground: ThemedColor? - unselected row text; null = mutedForeground token
fields.fontWeight: FontWeight? - selected row weight; null = w600
fields.fadeColor: ThemedColor? - edge fade base; null = background token
fields.perspective: double? - 3D amount when the perspective flag is on; null = 0.003
fields.surfaceColor: ThemedColor? - wheel container fill; null = background token
fields.separatorColor: ThemedColor? - column separators; null = border token

accessibility.keyboard: Tab reaches the wheel; ArrowUp/Down move the selection in the active column, ArrowLeft/Right switch column, PageUp/Down page by the visible row count, Home/End jump to the ends
accessibility.semantics: the picker is a labelled container; each row announces its label and selected state; disabled pickers dim to 50% opacity

sizes.wheel: 5 rows visible by default (visibleItems), 32px edge fades

notes: Each column is a ListWheelScrollView with a FixedExtentScrollController and FixedExtentScrollPhysics, so drag, mouse wheel and fling snap to row boundaries without extra physics code.
Looping repeats the items 10000 times and maps the controller index back with modulo, so the wheel never clamps; the selection callback reports the real item index.
The 3D look reuses ListWheelScrollView's perspective/diameterRatio; the flat default sets perspective to 0.
The selection callback is haptic-free by design: it reports the selected index of every column and never fires HapticFeedback, so the caller decides when to give feedback.
Tap-to-select wraps each row in a GestureDetector that animates the controller to the tapped item.
Controlled when value is set, uncontrolled with initialValue when it is null; the two are mutually exclusive by convention (value wins).
